- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 30d horizon.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overshoots; cap peak at 1.2x prior 18d high unless sentiment is strongly bearish.
- In high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model underreacts to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast to align with sentiment mean over last 5–7 days.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% over 3 consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = prior true + 0.8×(true - prior forecast).
- For 30d forecasts with low sentiment (≤0.33), model often underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast if sentiment remains flat or mildly bearish.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by >2% over 10+ days, increase forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment turns bullish or price stabilizes.
